scope: Theorem 6.8 of the manuscript “Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters” (preprints/Global-Arthur-Enhancements-of-Cuspidal-Excursion-Parameters-October-5-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 98c8561d3049c5b9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let t, H = ZL(t) and m be associated with a selected place as in Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2. After an etale base change on invariant holonomy functions and a saturated shrinking about the identity class, the Iwahori trace has a fully faithful coherent realization. Its composite with coherent duality, the covariant Koszul functor G0, and the change of degree by m-weight is contravariant and has the following properties. Its unit corresponds to P = M b Pb ∈ CohH (Y ), Y = {(u, e) ∈ UH × E+ : Ad(u)e = e}, where the Pb are the derived flag direct images in (6.16). The scheme Y is a classical complete intersection in the smooth affine scheme UH × E+. The hyperspecial unit is the retract B = OY of P under (6.23). The unsheared representation comparisons are (6.25); their internal algebra and scalar actions are (6.24). Before duality the slide on a label V is the matrix V (tu). The ordinary H-equivariant algebra End(P)op is the affine Hecke algebra with parameter r, pulled back along the etale map on its center. It has no higher cohomology, and its spherical corner is End(B) = O(UH)H. All these comparisons respect the matrix operations, homogeneous spherical maps, and neutral spectators of Proposition 5.3. They permit tests by every finite representation of H/Z(L). In the even sectors used below, a test of m-weight w changes cohomological degree from b to b + w; the other sectors use the stated parity adjustment. The ring comparisons preserve the open orbit and boundary over unipotent u. The covariant coherent and Koszul realizations extend fully faithfully to Ind-completions; duality is applied to the compact test objects. The same statements hold for finite products of selected places, with external test objects, separate parity sectors, and the sum of the m-weights.
